title: Forged committer dates can make history-based --at count early
description: Review of faq3.12 (2026-10-23): query --at (tiers since faq3.11, endorsements since faq3.12) uses the first-parent committer date to decide what was in effect at TIME. A fast-forwarded contributor commit with a forged GIT_COMMITTER_DATE can make a tier or endorsement count earlier than it was merged. Cheapest fix: clamp each first-parent commit's effective date to at least its first-parent ancestor's (monotonic), so a backdated commit cannot precede what came before it; alternatively require --no-ff merges into the registry (process, not code). Decide and record in DESIGN TRQP bridge Time.
acceptance_criteria: Test: a commit with a committer date earlier than its parent's does not make its records count before the parent's date; DESIGN states the rule.
notes: Code done (core-dates unit): effective = max(own, first parent's effective) on every commit; a commit off HEAD's first-parent line counts from the first first-parent commit that has it (landed), so --no-ff-merged deletions end at the merge; check errors on a commit dated > FUTURE_SLACK (5 min) ahead. Tests: test_backdated_deletion_ends_the_tier_at_its_parents_date, test_deletion_merged_with_no_ff_ends_the_tier_at_the_merge, test_merge_counts_from_its_first_parent_not_its_branch, test_commit_dated_in_the_future_is_refused, test_committer_date_out_of_range (far attribution), test_backdated_promotion_counts_from_its_parents_date. Remaining: DESIGN states the rule + --no-ff policy (docs unit doc_changes). Open question for Mark: foxtrot fast-forward (contributor merge with own branch as first parent) is not caught by any date clamp; only the --no-ff policy covers it.
close_reason: Mark's (c): effective dates monotonic along first-parent, side-branch commits count from their merge, check refuses committer dates >5 min ahead (26f41f4, tests in test_check_history/test_export/test_query); DESIGN Effective dates + --no-ff (eeaf899, 8d18473)
